hypothesis: SIC-C-c asks whether restricting to a specific inductive-bias hypothesis class can restore uniform polynomial-in-d_Z sample complexity for the continuous-case learnability problem of paper section 2.5b (Theorem 6). Instrument 8 answered yes for the linear-ICA class; this instrument (instrument 9) answers the same for the sparse-mixing / independent-mechanism analysis (IMA) class (Gresele et al. 2021). Setup: latent Z with independent Laplace(0, 1) marginals; mixing A drawn as (i) a Haar-orthogonal Q via signed QR, (ii) multiplied entry-wise by a Bernoulli(s) sparse mask with sparsity s in {0.5, 0.25} and rank-deficiency retries (or a keep-diagonal fallback), (iii) re-orthonormalised via a second signed QR; observation X = A * Z. Algorithm: sklearn FastICA (parallel, logcosh, whiten='unit-variance', max_iter=2000, tol=1e-6, random_state=trial). Metric: Amari index on P = W * A. Predictions: (a) averaged Amari <= 0.02 at N = 10000 for every d_Z in {2, 4, 6, 8} and every sparsity in {0.5, 0.25}; (b) sparser (s=0.25) recovery is at least as good as denser (s=0.5) modulo a 0.01 tolerance for every d_Z, witnessing that the independent-mechanism inductive bias is compatible with (or actively helps) recovery; (c) for each sparsity the smallest N reaching averaged Amari <= 0.03 grows only polynomially in d_Z (fitted log-log slope b <= 3.0); (d) at every (d_Z, s) the Amari(N) curve is nonincreasing modulo a 0.01 wobble tolerance.

gates.SICA_FASTICA_CONVERGES_AT_LARGEST_N_BOTH: At N = 10000, the Amari index averaged over 8 trials is <= 0.02 for every d_Z in {2, 4, 6, 8} and every sparsity in {0.5, 0.25}.
gates.SICA_SPARSER_MIXING_IMPROVES_OR_MATCHES_: At N = 10000, averaged Amari at sparsity s = 0.25 minus averaged Amari at sparsity s = 0.5 is <= 0.01 for every d_Z in {2, 4, 6, 8} (sparser recovery is at least as good as denser, modulo the 0.01 finite-sample tolerance).
gates.SICA_SAMPLE_COMPLEXITY_POLYNOMIAL_IN_D_Z: For every sparsity in {0.5, 0.25} and every d_Z in {2, 4, 6, 8} there is a smallest N in the sweep {200, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000} with averaged Amari <= 0.03; the linear regression log(N_needed(d_Z)) = a + b * log(d_Z) has fitted slope b <= 3.0 for both sparsities.
gates.SICA_AMARI_MONOTONE_IN_N_AT_EVERY_D_Z_AN: For every (d_Z, sparsity) pair the averaged Amari curve is nonincreasing in N modulo a numerical tolerance of 0.01 (i.e. amari_mean at N_{i+1} <= amari_mean at N_i + 0.01).

compute.sampling: Per (d_Z, trial, sparsity) draw a Haar-orthogonal Q via signed QR, apply a Bernoulli(s) mask (retrying up to 32 times if the mask has an empty row/column or the masked matrix is rank-deficient; on persistent failure fall back to keep_diag which forces the diagonal mask to 1), re-orthonormalise via a second signed QR, and sample Laplace(0, 1) latents Z of size (max(N_VALUES), d_Z); every smaller N reuses the first N samples of the same draw as a prefix. sklearn FastICA(parallel, logcosh, whiten='unit-variance', max_iter=2000, tol=1e-6, random_state=trial). SeedSequence keyed by [BASE_SEED=0, d_Z, trial, int(round(s*1000))].
